texts: mixed: the kind and the place come through (Stilllight Station is a lantern-station, located at the Sunken Cove), but the definite predicate 'the lantern-station' — the claim that it is the one and only lantern-station there — has no carrier in the instruction set, so the parse records only that it is *a* lantern-station. If that uniqueness is part of what you mean, write 'Only the Stilllight Station is a lantern-station at the Sunken Cove.'; if it is not, 'The Stilllight Station is a lantern-station at the Sunken Cove.' gives the same parse as now with nothing lost.
good. the name, the station kind and the evaluative 'demanding' each land as their own atom, with nothing invented.
good. parses as a fireable universal rule — one fearing state per Keeper, with the Stilllight Station as what is feared and the 'every' quantifier recorded.
